summary: Consistent hashing enables distributed systems to scale servers up or down while moving only a tiny fraction of keys. Adding virtual nodes ensures the data load stays evenly balanced across the cluster even when machines fail or differ in capacity.

key_points.title: The Modulo Trap (Why Naive Hashing Fails)
key_points.core_idea: Using `hash(key) % N` ties every data key's location directly to the total server count `N`. If a single node joins or crashes, `N` changes and nearly every key hashes to a new server, triggering a massive cache stampede.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: Musical chairs where adding one extra chair forces every single person in the room to get up and scramble to a brand-new seat.

key_points.title: The Hash Ring & Clockwise Walk
key_points.core_idea: Both server IDs and data keys are hashed onto the same fixed circular integer space (like `0` to `2^32 - 1`). To find which server stores a key, start at the key's hash position and walk clockwise around the ring until you hit the first server node.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: Dropping packages onto a giant 12-hour clock face; each package slides clockwise along the rim until it falls into the next open server bucket.

key_points.title: Minimal Disruption on Scale or Failure
key_points.core_idea: When a node is added or removed on the ring, only the keys sitting on the arc between that node and its immediate counterclockwise neighbor need to move. On average, only `K / N` keys relocate while the rest stay untouched.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: Slotting a new tollbooth onto a circular highway—only the cars right behind the new booth divert into it, while traffic across the rest of the loop keeps cruising.

key_points.title: Virtual Nodes (Vnodes) for Even Balance
key_points.core_idea: With only a few physical servers, random hashing leaves uneven gaps on the ring and creates hotspots. Assigning each physical server many virtual nodes scattered across the ring slices the keyspace into fine, interleaved segments for uniform load distribution and weighted capacity.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: Instead of three goalies standing clumped together on a giant circular field, each goalie spawns dozens of hologram clones spaced evenly around the entire perimeter.
